note: Authored operating rows for performance-paid faceless AI UGC and creator-reward campaigns: launch readiness, creator selection, payout controls, funnel diagnosis, cohort testing, scorecard fields, organic-to-paid handoff, and operator communication. These rows paraphrase useful mechanisms from the user-supplied promotional article 'This is how we scaled RIZZ app to $5,000,000/year with AI UGC (The Complete Guide)' but deliberately omit its unverified revenue, spend, network-size, CPM, view-band, cohort-size, ROAS, and budget claims. They are starting hypotheses, not measured results. The full playbook lives in the shared skills shelf as content-rewards-viral-app-campaign. Hard rules: no payout for invalid traffic, no fabricated engagement or proof, no public humiliation, no creator outreach/spend/publishing without approval, no paid reuse without documented rights, and no scaling without downstream attribution and a hard loss cap. Slots are UPPERCASE so an unfilled template trips the deliverable acceptance gate.
omitted: Current provider prices, creator-network size, platform capabilities, universal view thresholds, fixed cohort sizes, fixed test windows, fixed ROAS targets, and fixed daily budgets are intentionally absent because they are volatile or only vendor-claimed. Resolve them from current primary evidence and the app's own economics.

readinessGates.pass: the result is understandable in one frame or a short native clip
readinessGates.block: the promise stays generic or requires a long explanation

readinessGates.pass: install through paid conversion is measured by source
readinessGates.block: only views or aggregate downloads are visible

readinessGates.pass: cohort retention or conservative contribution value is observed
readinessGates.block: revenue potential is inferred from top-line pricing alone

readinessGates.pass: creator, account, post, click, install, and downstream events reconcile
readinessGates.block: the operator cannot connect a post to business outcomes

readinessGates.pass: an owned converting format exists or a bounded discovery test is defined
readinessGates.block: the plan assumes a large roster will discover product-market fit

readinessGates.pass: budget, payout, fraud, rights, appeal, and stop rules are written
readinessGates.block: launch terms allow uncapped spend or ambiguous paid reuse

creatorCriteria.evidence: rights-respecting examples showing the same structural format, not merely the same category
plausible organic history and engagement with no obvious bought-view, engagement-pod, impersonation, or policy pattern
follows claim, disclosure, rights, naming, demo, CTA, and submission requirements
meets an agreed cadence without repetitive spam, quality collapse, or undisclosed delegation
clear first frame, tight pacing, mobile-safe captions, readable app demo, and coherent hook stack
responds to feedback, submits clean evidence, respects corrections, and surfaces source-linked format ideas

launchPaths.useWhen: the operator has an original post with attributable conversion evidence
launchPaths.test: use a small cohort to test whether the structure transfers across creators

launchPaths.useWhen: no format has attributable conversion evidence
launchPaths.test: cap the cohort and maximum loss, test distinct format families, and treat the spend as research

payoutControls.rule: publish the source, counting window, invalid-traffic filters, paid-boost treatment, and late-adjustment policy before launch
set a clearly disclosed minimum payable amount or aggregation policy so valid micro-earnings do not disappear into processing ambiguity
cap payout per creator and campaign so one account cannot consume the budget before review
set the maximum approved payout plus operating spend before the first post; exceeding it requires a new approval
reward verified installs, activations, qualified trials, paid customers, or retained value only when attribution and fraud controls support it
show the rejection reason, evidence class, response window, reviewer, and final disposition without exposing fraud-detection secrets
server-side verified events and the approved terms determine payout; creator screenshots and local UI state are evidence, not authority

diagnosticLadder.pattern: healthy delivery with weak initial attention
diagnosticLadder.suspect: hook, first frame, format-audience fit, or account eligibility
diagnosticLadder.nextTest: hold the body constant and test several hooks after checking platform diagnostics

diagnosticLadder.suspect: pacing, dead space, story tension, creator execution, or reveal timing
diagnosticLadder.nextTest: recut the middle, move proof earlier, and compare creators on the same brief

diagnosticLadder.pattern: strong views with weak clicks or installs
diagnosticLadder.suspect: low product intent, unclear demo, CTA timing, caption naming, or store mismatch
diagnosticLadder.nextTest: add a truthful app demo and explicit next step, then align the store promise

diagnosticLadder.pattern: installs with weak activation or payment
diagnosticLadder.suspect: onboarding, paywall, trial terms, value delivery, or product retention
diagnosticLadder.nextTest: stop creative scale and fix the downstream funnel

diagnosticLadder.pattern: paid customers with weak retention or high refunds
diagnosticLadder.suspect: expectation mismatch, claim quality, or product value
diagnosticLadder.nextTest: stop scale, audit the promise, and repair retention before buying more traffic

cohortRules.detail: a cohort tests one hook, first frame, format, creator segment, CTA, or product-demonstration change at a time
list creators, accounts, platforms, posts, start time, and exclusions before results are reviewed
record the maximum payout and operating spend that can accrue without a new approval
choose the review window from platform delivery and downstream event delay, not a copied fixed number
reserve an explicit test share while a winner runs; change the share when decay speed, test cost, or confidence changes
add creators only when downstream conversion, payout efficiency, and traffic quality remain acceptable after the declared window
retire or rework a format when normalized hold, conversion, or payout efficiency degrades across enough comparable posts—not merely because it feels old

scoreboardFields.role: first-frame and hook diagnostic at the platform-supported interval
acquisition outcome reconciled to creator and post
offer and paywall diagnostic where applicable
customer outcome, separated from free acquisition
net value over a stated cohort window
approved cost after verification and disputes
payout efficiency at install, activation, trial, customer, and retained-value levels

paidHandoff.evidence: documented paid-media rights, authorization duration, territories, edit rights, identity, and compensation
final caption/post authorization or an approved editable master with a known takedown path
current AI, sponsorship, category-claim, music, likeness, and platform review
test install and revenue events reconcile through the selected measurement path
conservative contribution value, target acquisition ceiling, payback window, and refund assumptions
creative matrix, daily and lifetime cap, delayed-conversion window, and kill/hold/scale rules
human-approved account, geography, campaign mode, identity, budget, creatives, dates, and operator authority

antiPatterns.why: attention without attributable installs, customers, or retained value can be expensive vanity
copied view bands, CPMs, cohort sizes, test windows, and ROAS targets ignore the app's distribution and economics

antiPatterns.pattern: large roster before a bounded test
antiPatterns.why: marginal creator value can decline while payout exposure and operational noise rise
check account eligibility, policy status, delivery, hook, and comparable posts before blaming an opaque platform penalty
screenshots can be stale or manipulated and do not replace authoritative platform and attribution evidence
public standards are useful; naming and shaming individual creators is coercive, damages trust, and adds no diagnostic value
reuse structural lessons while keeping scripts, footage, voice, likeness, branding, and claims original or licensed
test new hooks and formats in a declared cohort before exposing the full budget
renegotiating after a post wins creates leverage, delay, takedown, and consent risk

antiPatterns.pattern: upload every clip without a cap
antiPatterns.why: organic underperformance does not preclude paid success, but paid exploration still needs a deliberate matrix and maximum loss
